newsitem.title: UK: US stocks firm in London, buoyed by weaker dollar.
newsitem.headline: US stocks firm in London, buoyed by weaker dollar.

text.p: U.S. stocks were firmer across the board in London on Monday as a weaker U.S. dollar lured European investors, dealers said.

Gain in London came on the back of Friday's stunning performance on Wall Street, where the Dow surged to a record, leaping 130.49 points to 7,435.78. The rally was ignited by U.S. employment data for May, which pointed to solid non-inflationary economic growth.
"It's hard to believe after what happened on Friday. Normally, the market would take a bit of a rest, but the dollar is making (U.S. stocks) look cheap to Europeans," said one London dealer.

High technology stocks were most active, with shares in International Business Machines Corp gaining $1/4 to $85-3/4 in London, after jumping $2-5/8 in New York on Friday. The computer giant is set to announce upgrades on its microprocessor-based mainframe today.
Shares in COMPAQ Computer Corp were up $1/4 to $103-1/8. COMPAQ is expected to unveil a new Intel-based computer workstation today. Intel Corp added $3/4 to $146-3/4 in London.
Elsewhere, shares in Philip Morris Cos Inc advanced $3/8 to $43 on hopes an industry wide tobacco settlement will limit punitive damages, dealers said.
Shares in Coca-Cola Co climbed $3/8 to $68-1/8, while Merck and Co Inc rose $1/8 to $92-1/2 after U.S. financial weekly Barron's tipped the shares as a buy.
Shares in Chrysler Corp firmed $1/4 to $33 after upbeat comments from Barron's, dealers said.
General Motors Corp shares, meanwhile, were up $1/8 to $57 while Ford Motor Co shares were unchanged at $38-1/8.
In other trading, June S&P 500 index futures were off 0.90 at 861.60 on Globex at 1027 GMT, while June long bond futures eased 6/32 to 111-14/32. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 5106
